key_insight: PhysDial shows that training on trajectories with changing physical conditions helps learned PDE simulators respond to interventions rather than merely accept condition inputs.
engineering_relevance: More responsive learned simulators could support control, design, and scenario studies involving changes in forcing or physical parameters.
method: Adapts a pretrained video diffusion transformer to eight two-dimensional PDE families.
Encodes coefficients alongside noise level, condition fields as reference frames, and equations as text prompts.
Uses within-trajectory interventions and counterfactual solver branches to train and evaluate responses to changed conditions.
evidence_signal: In Kolmogorov flow, within-trajectory switches made up about 5% of training samples and halved post-change error for forcing wavenumber or amplitude at matched compute.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to two-dimensional PDEs, and reliable responses to unseen interventions may require additional condition-changing training trajectories.
paper_title: PhysDial: Adapting Pretrained Video Models for PDE Simulation under Changing Physical Conditions
